sect1.title: SMTP Authentication
sect1.para: Zend_Mail supports the use of SMTP authentication, which can be enabled be passing the 'auth' parameter to the configuration array in the Zend_Mail_Transport_Smtp constructor. The available built-in authentication methods are PLAIN, LOGIN and CRAM-MD5 which all expect a 'username' and 'password' value in the configuration array.

example.title: Enabling authentication within Zend_Mail_Transport_Smtp

note.title: Authentication types
note.para: The authentication type is case-insensitive but has no punctuation. E.g. to use CRAM-MD5 you would pass 'auth' => 'crammd5' in the Zend_Mail_Transport_Smtp constructor.

sect2.title: OAuth 2.0 (XOAUTH2)
sect2.para: Gmail and Microsoft 365 no longer accept a password for SMTP; they expect an OAuth 2.0 access token, sent with the XOAUTH2 mechanism. Pass 'auth' => 'xoauth2' together with the mailbox in 'username' and the token in 'accessToken'. Obtaining the token (the OAuth 2.0 authorization flow with the provider) and refreshing it before it expires is the job of the application; the transport only uses the token it is given, so a new transport (or a new token) is needed after a refresh.

example.title: Sending through Gmail with an access token

sect2.para: When the server rejects the token, the Zend_Mail_Protocol_Exception carries the final reply of the server (e.g. "535 5.7.8 Username and Password not accepted") and, in parentheses, the reason the server sent in its challenge (a JSON object with the status and the required scope).
